title: Goner: early prototype of my 2D metroidvania is now on itch.io
author: _serse
selftext:
Hi everyone! I'm the solo dev behind Goner, a 2D metroidvania built in Godot, and the first build is now up on itch.io.



What is it?

An emotional adventure in metroidvania style to rescue your family. This trip will take you in dangerous places...



What to expect right now

This is an early draft of the project. You'll find the first 2 areas but it's only the surface. The world of Goner hides a much bigger story, and I'll be revealing it piece by piece through updates.



What's coming



What I'd love feedback on

Atmosphere, map layout and difficulty



Bug reports, thoughts and ideas are all welcome. Updates will be posted on the [itch.io](http://itch.io) page.



👉 [https://serse12.itch.io/goner](https://serse12.itch.io/goner)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Okay. Foundationally, I think think has some promise.

The writing is... extremely AI, in a bad way, and that's a problem if you want this to emotionally resonate with the player. There's also some worldbuilding that is... odd.

So, the world was peaceful for a very long time. Okay. Why, then, are there knights and blacksmiths that are skilled in making sword? Like, that suggests there is demand for both a caste of martial nobility and also demand for costly armament. There can always be reasons why a peacful world wants those things, but it feels like this wasn't reall considered since it's not woven into the anything.

When you are doing the visual storytelling with the narrative, the images shown are both kind of generic and also clash with the atmosphere of the text. The text says our family was disappeared in the aftermath of the monster invasion... but while it says this, it just shows a generic medieval fantasy indoor setting with a mangled AI generated sword sitting idly on the table. The lighting and colors are neutral.

This is the emotional core of the player's motivation - the imagery needs to convery the sense of grief, rage, emptiness, shock, etc, that the player is supposed to be resonating with in order to feel like this is their quest.

Please take a look at this opening, from the game The Last Spell: 

[The Last Spell - Opening Sequence](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YcqfTYJvKmk)

Very similar idea to your in terms of just simple text against background imagery with a very basic premise. But they absolutely nail the emotional beats, the sense of atmosphere, the character of the world the player will be engaging with.

'It was extremely peaceful for a long time, but then monsters appeared' can be extremely engaging, but it requires good set-up and delivery for the player to buy in.

The world also won't feel like a world if things are simply described without having proper nouns. Events are never catalogued as 'the time the ground opened and monsters came out'. That event would be given some sort of name, and the date it happened on would have attached weight. Think of '9/11' , or 'D Day', or 'Hurricane Katrina' , or 'Apollo 11'. 

  
Gameplay wise, it feels... okay. I really disagree with the default keyboard layout; reaching for X and C is extremely awkward when using WASD, and I sure how the S+J attack doesn't do anything because that's never actually happening.

The tells for the boss are weird. The red flash isn't bright enough to notice, and the boss doesn't freeze frames or anything while the flashing plays so it blurs into the motion. Telegraphing the attack with certain animation frames is just always going to feel better than waiting for a color flash and is more accessible for anyone with color blindness.

I agree with the initial level design being very linear with a few tantalizing rewards for when you get the next tier of level traversal... but I also think it is slightly too linear. This is a matter of taste, but I prefer when a Metroidvania sets the tone for me, just a little bit, interms of traversal but offering a very simple amount of traversal choice right from the start.

replies.author: _serse
replies.body:
I really apreciate this comment. Thank you very much.  
It is first of all a Proof Of Concept, I'm writing the lore right now! I just wanted to see if the arts are apreciables and things like that.   
I will work a LOT on dialogues and the history.  
In this first version and world I didn't want to make the game difficult.   
You are right on a lot of points.  But there are few things that i don't want to spend time on. Exaple: Naming the events (it's not really important to me, it doesn't add anything to the game), the peaceful reign always need an army in a medieval era in my opinion and it's ok that in a medieval town there is a merchant selling swords. It is really common. In the medieval era as a king you should always invest for your army. Invasions can always happen.  
I'm sorry for the images/videos but i have no money to improve them and they really cost a lot!  
Everything in the NEXT update! stay tuned!

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body: Well, if the introductory worldbuilding and text don't matter to you, that's totally fine - just cut it, then. Get rid of the introduction, and just start the player out as a knight in a world without a bunch of fluff. The player doesn't need any context to understand, 'I am knight, this is fantasy setting, I kill orcs and grab loot'.
